llm.summary: The skill's claimed purpose (generate/enforce constraints from observed failures) matches what the SKILL.md asks for and it requests no credentials or installs, but there are small metadata inconsistencies and no code to inspect, so verify dependencies before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description align with the instructions: the skill generates constraints from observations, enforces them, and writes results to workspace paths. However the metadata contains small inconsistencies (homepage under live-neon but repository field lists leegitw/constraint-engine; install examples mention context-verifier in addition to failure-memory). These mismatches are not show-stoppers but reduce confidence and merit confirmation before install.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is instruction-only and explicitly scopes file access to declared config (.openclaw/.claude) and workspace paths (output/constraints/, output/hooks/). It claims no external network calls and no model invocation (disable-model-invocation: true). There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or to exfiltrate secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or archive downloads are present (instruction-only). The SKILL.md shows example openclaw install commands for this skill and related skills; because nothing is fetched by this skill itself there is minimal install risk. You should still verify what the referenced dependencies (e.g., leegitw/failure-memory, context-verifier) do before installing them.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths beyond its own config files. That is proportionate to a workspace-scoped constraint/enforcement helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and disable-model-invocation is true, so the skill will not be force-included or autonomously invoked by the model. It writes only to its declared workspace paths, which is consistent with its purpose.

llm.guidance: This instruction-only skill appears coherent and relatively low-risk, but you should: (1) confirm the correct source repository (metadata shows live-neon and leegitw inconsistencies) before running openclaw install; (2) inspect the code and behavior of any dependency it recommends (leegitw/failure-memory and any context-verifier) — those will determine actual runtime behavior; (3) review the .openclaw/.claude config files it reads and the output/constraints/ directory it writes to, and ensure sensitive data is not placed there; (4) because there is no code in the package to audit, prefer installing into an isolated workspace or test agent first; and (5) if you need higher assurance, ask the publisher for the exact repository URL and a minimal reproducible example so you can review the implementation before trusting enforcement in production.
